blocks.label: introduction
content: # Inlined Capture
Load this module for `tarav-hugentics --capture --inline <SURFACE>`.
`Inlined.Capture` is an Agent-operated Chatlas-context Breadcrumb workflow.
Its ordinary route leaves compact opaque Breadcrumb labels beside useful
fragments of one `Product.Surface`; each label has a typed attachment to one
relevant Chatlas `User.Turn`. Its `--audit` route checks retained Breadcrumbs
without mutation. A later Agent may peek around resolved Turns and selectively
digest them into richer context. Breadcrumbs are not themselves a digest,
Diagram capture, grounding Assertion, approval claim, or completeness claim.
Read the selected surface's project instructions first. The ordinary standalone
invocation authorizes one bounded edit of that surface. A composing workflow may
invoke the same mechanics for each Product.Surface it is already authorized to
modify. The audit invocation authorizes no mutation: do not edit the surface,
update Chatlas, create Diagram records, or write a retained report.
Breadcrumbs have embedded and external placement. Embedded placement uses
native comments in Markdown, Python, TypeScript (`.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mts`,
`.cts`; a draft convention) and TOML. External placement leaves the surface
untouched and retains its file, observed line and exact fragment in the
registry. JSON is always read-only for the Breadcrumb workflow and uses
external placement. Other readable text can use that same route.

blocks.label: routes
content: ## Routes
### Capture
```text
tarav-hugentics --capture --inline <SURFACE>
Discover relevant User Turns, insert provisional markers, and submit them
through the `chatlas-context` Breadcrumb workflow.
### Audit
```text
tarav-hugentics --capture --inline --audit <SURFACE>
Inventory and assess existing Breadcrumbs in exactly one surface. Audit is
read-only and stops after reporting its findings. It does not assess whether
the surface has complete conversational coverage.

blocks.label: surface-contract
content: ## Native surface contract
A provisional marker carries the derived eight-character session alias and an
ordinary 16-character User-Turn hash prefix. Put it at the exact position
materially contextualized by that Turn, using native comments for embedded placement:
```python
# tarav.context 4571385e:dd358589d092f9dd
```md
<!-- tarav.context 4571385e:dd358589d092f9dd -->
```ts
// tarav.context 4571385e:dd358589d092f9dd
TOML uses `# tarav.context <alias>:<prefix>` comments. Basic, literal and
multiline strings are inactive, including any `#` text inside them.
JSON uses external placement. Do not add metadata fields or markers to it.
Embedded JSON submission is rejected before workflow or registry writes,
even if its language is overridden. Existing JSON labels remain readable
for inspection; the workflow does not remove or rewrite them.
External placement registers the same Breadcrumb identity and typed
attachments. Its location observation retains an exact single-line fragment.
Resolution first checks the observed line, then searches that file. A unique
matching line resolves; several matches are ambiguous. A missing line or file
reports an external anchor missing, retaining identity and attachments.
A maintainer supplies replacement coordinates explicitly; a failed lookup
never means the Breadcrumb was deleted. Old observations remain retained.
Never place embedded markers inside strings, examples, fenced code, or other inactive
syntax. Python markers are tokenizer-confirmed comments. TypeScript markers
are `//` line comments confirmed by a small lexer that skips strings, template
literals, regular expressions and block comments; block comments never carry
markers. Markdown markers attach
to the immediately preceding Markdown block; consecutive markers attach to that
same block.
The alias is the first eight lowercase hexadecimal characters of the neutral
Chatlas session identity. It is derived, never chosen or rebound. Markdown may
retain one or more session declarations near the top of the document:
```md
<!-- tarav.sessions
A declaration retains the alias, `<provider>:<native-session-id>`, and full
identity hash. The identity hash is authoritative. Reuse a matching declaration
and treat disagreement as a POI. For a surface without declarations, pass the
exact provider and session ID to submission. One explicit session can resolve
only markers carrying that session's alias.
Embedded submission replaces every active provisional marker with the corresponding
opaque `tarav.breadcrumb <prefix>` label in the same native embedding:
the first 12 characters of the Breadcrumb's 64-character ID, which the
registry keeps. The ordinary Product.Surface remains authoritative.
A label names the one registered ID it starts with. A label matching several
IDs is an error that lists them; Tarav never picks one, whatever the retained
positions or attachments suggest. Submission reports such a collision rather
than writing it. After choosing the intended Breadcrumb, lengthen its label
one character at a time (13, 14, 15, ...) until it is unique. Full
64-character labels remain valid.
<!-- tarav.breadcrumb 3796ae36306e -->

blocks.label: capture-workflow
content: ## Capture workflow
1. Read the selected Product.Surface, its project instructions, and its supported
native embedding convention. Inspect existing session declarations where the
convention supports them.
2. When the current chat is in scope, resolve and refresh it once through
`tarav-chatlas-my-session-id`. Reuse its returned provider, native session
ID, and neutral Chatlas identity; do not perform another update. Derive the
alias from that identity hash. Reuse or add a declaration when supported;
otherwise retain the exact provider and session ID for submission.
3. Discover candidate User Turns from each exact session with the compact
timestamped ledger when their hashes are not already known:
```bash
tarav chatlas render \
--provider <provider> \
--session-id <native-session-id> \
--side user \
--order newest \
--limit 50 \
--renderer Chatlas.Turn.Ledger.Renderer
The ledger aids navigation; the Agent still decides semantic relevance.
4. Group selected Turns by exact session. Resolve each ordered group through
the shared Chatlas Query engine; Renderers never perform selection.
For JSON or another read-only surface, select its line and exact fragment
and run external submission. No provisional marker goes into the file:
```bash
tarav breadcrumbs submit chatlas-context --placement external \
--surface <SURFACE> --line <LINE> --fragment '<EXACT_FRAGMENT>' \
--provider <PROVIDER> --session-id <SESSION_ID> \
--turn-hash-prefix <USER_TURN_PREFIX> --json
Continue at step 8. This retains the exact cited Turn before registration.
5. For embedded placement, produce markers in native comment syntax. For
Markdown, the named Renderer can produce the reference comments:
```bash
tarav chatlas render \
--provider <provider> \
--session-id <native-session-id> \
--turn-hash-prefix <prefix> \
[--turn-hash-prefix <prefix> ...] \
--renderer Inlined.Capture.Markdown.Reference.Renderer
The Renderer derives the alias from the resolved session; it takes no
Renderer options. For Python, use tokenizer-valid `# tarav.context` comments
carrying that same derived alias and selected Turn prefix; for TypeScript,
`// tarav.context` line comments. TOML uses `#` comments.
6. Insert each provisional comment at the exact materially contextualized
position. Several markers may be distributed across the surface; a resolved
Turn group need not be inserted contiguously.
7. Once the embedded surface content is final, run this exactly once:
```bash
tarav breadcrumbs submit chatlas-context --surface <SURFACE> \
[--provider <PROVIDER> --session-id <SESSION_ID>] --json
Submission must
retain each Breadcrumb, position observation, and typed Chatlas attachment
before replacing its provisional marker. Exact cited Turns, Messages and
supporting Events are retained as validated Chatlas snapshots so later
normalization changes cannot silently replace the cited material.
8. Run `tarav breadcrumbs audit chatlas-context --surface <SURFACE> --json`.
Use its mechanical findings for label positions, typed attachments, and
referenced User Turns. Then inspect semantic placement and report the new
Breadcrumbs plus unresolved POIs.
If submission cannot register, typically because a sandbox prevents writing
to the Tarav data folder, leave the read-only trace. Keep the provisional
`tarav.context` markers where they are and keep their session resolvable.
A Markdown surface carries its `tarav.sessions` declaration. A surface
without one, such as Python or TypeScript, relies on the same alias being declared in
the related Wiki Note or Impl.Req.
Do not remove the markers or invent Breadcrumb labels, and report the
registration as pending, not as done. A later session that can write runs the
same `submit` and `audit` commands on the surface; nothing has to be guessed
while the declaration is intact.
A failed submission leaves the surface unchanged, and the Project check
keeps reporting Notes that still carry provisional markers.
When an audit reports stale label positions because lines moved, rerun it
with `--refresh-positions`. It appends repaired position observations for
uniquely located Breadcrumbs and leaves the surface unchanged.
For external placement this records the uniquely resolved fragment's current
line. A read-only audit or resolve never appends observations.
If the selected fragment disappears or remains ambiguous, its maintainer
can explicitly provide a replacement location and selection:
```bash
tarav breadcrumbs relocate --label <BREADCRUMB_ID> --surface <FILE> \
--line <LINE> --fragment '<EXACT_FRAGMENT>' --json
This preserves identity, attachments and old observations. It never rewrites
the source file or automatically chooses another semantic target.
Use 16 hexadecimal characters as the ordinary prefix length. Resolution is
bounded by the exact session, so collisions are uncommon. If a prefix is
ambiguous, inspect only its matched candidates and lengthen that reference. If
it is missing, report a nonblocking POI rather than guessing.
The integration workflow uses Chatlas Query for exact resolution, a Renderer
or native convention for provisional surface syntax, and the generic Breadcrumb
transaction for
retention and label replacement. A composing workflow uses this complete path
after it finishes each selected surface; it does not restate or fork the
mechanics. Inlined Capture adds no alias registry, automatic
Git-history audit, Diagram record, Assertion score, or generalized impact map.

blocks.label: audit-contract
content: ## Audit contract
The generic audit protocol asks the same bounded questions for any supported
surface while leaving syntax recognition to that surface's convention:
1. Which context sources or sessions are declared?
2. Which Breadcrumb labels and leftover provisional markers occur, and where?
3. Does every Breadcrumb resolve to exactly one observed surface position?
4. Does every Breadcrumb carry one valid typed Chatlas-context attachment?
5. Does that attachment resolve to the intended User Turn, and is its local
placement semantically plausible?
6. Which conditions need Agent or User attention?
Mechanical resolution does not establish semantic relevance, correctness,
authorship, approval, completeness, or exclusive support. Attachment judgment
remains Agent work.

blocks.label: audit-workflow
content: ## Audit workflow
1. Read the selected surface, its project instructions, and its native
embedding convention. Do not enter the ordinary capture workflow.
2. Run `tarav breadcrumbs audit chatlas-context --surface <SURFACE> --json`.
This read-only command inventories active labels and provisional markers,
resolves positions, validates typed attachments, and checks retained User
Turns without refreshing Chatlas.
3. Inspect every mechanical finding and the returned Breadcrumb entries.
Continue past recoverable problems so one audit exposes the whole bounded
surface.
4. Inspect local placement according to the native convention. Markdown labels
attach to the immediately preceding block; Python, TypeScript and TOML labels
must be confirmed comments. External anchors must match their registered
line fragment; missing and ambiguous external anchors require maintenance.
JSON is read-only; existing embedded labels are inspection history. Report orphaned
or suspicious placements; do not repair them.
5. Return one compact in-chat report and stop. Include the surface,
specialization used, declaration count, Breadcrumb count, exact-resolution
count, and POIs with useful source locations.
Recognize the native provisional-marker and Breadcrumb forms specified above,
plus Markdown session declarations when present. Provisional Turn prefixes
ordinarily use 16 lowercase hexadecimal characters; Breadcrumb labels carry
an ID prefix of 12 to 64 characters, ordinarily 12.
Report at least these conditions when present:
- malformed or conflicting session declarations;
- Breadcrumb labels matching several Breadcrumbs;
- a declaration missing its identity hash, or whose alias is not that hash's
first 8 characters;
- malformed or leftover provisional markers;
- malformed Breadcrumb labels;
- missing or ambiguous observed positions;
- missing, multiple, or invalid typed Chatlas-context attachments;
- unavailable source sessions;
- missing or amended referenced Turns;
- attachments resolving to an Agent rather than a User Turn;
- Breadcrumbs placed inside inactive syntax or at a position whose relevance is
doubtful.
An unavailable target is a POI, not permission to update provider data or
guess a replacement. A semantically questionable attachment is likewise a POI,
not a verdict that the surface is wrong.
